rows.rule: $15,000,000 filing threshold / basic exclusion for decedents dying in 2026.
rows.impact: An estate (all assets incl. both houses, cash, securities) at or below this amount owes no federal estate tax.
rows.source: IRS — Estate tax (filing threshold table)

rows.topic: Working Families Tax Cuts (P.L. 119-21) set the 2026 amount
rows.rule: P.L. 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, amended IRC §2010(c)(3) to a $15,000,000 basic exclusion for 2026.
rows.status_as_of: Enacted law; no scheduled sunset stated on the IRS page
rows.impact: Replaces the pre-2026 expectation that the exclusion would roughly halve. Future Congresses can still amend it.
rows.source: IRS — What's new, Estate and gift tax

rows.topic: Estate tax exclusion (2027 deaths) and annual gift exclusion
rows.rule: $15,480,000 basic exclusion for 2027 deaths; annual gift exclusion $20,000 for 2027 (up from $19,000 in 2026). IR-2026-133, Nov. 5, 2026; Rev. Proc. 2026-35.
rows.impact: Confirms the exclusion is inflation-indexed after 2026 (+3.2% for 2027). Basis for the 2028–2050 scenario projection.
rows.source: IRS — IR-2026-133 (2027 inflation adjustments)

rows.topic: Estate tax rate above the exclusion
rows.rule: Unified rate schedule tops out at 40% on taxable amounts over $1,000,000 (Form 706 Table A). With an exclusion above $1M, each dollar over the exclusion is taxed at 40%.
rows.impact: Tax = 40% x (taxable estate - available exclusion) when the estate exceeds the exclusion.
rows.source: IRS — Instructions for Form 706 (07/2026), Table A

rows.rule: A surviving spouse can receive the deceased spouse's unused exclusion only if elected on a timely filed Form 706 (simplified late-election relief: Rev. Proc. 2022-32).
rows.impact: Can roughly double the shelter for the second death (2 x $15,000,000 in 2026 terms) — but only if Form 706 is filed at the first death.
rows.source: IRS — Estate tax page; Instructions for Form 706 (portability)

rows.topic: Step-up in basis for inherited property
rows.rule: Basis of inherited property is generally fair market value on the date of death (or alternate valuation date if elected on Form 706), whether or not Form 706 is filed.
rows.impact: Selling an inherited house soon after death produces little or no capital gain; most of the decades of appreciation is never taxed as income.
rows.source: IRS — Gifts & inheritances FAQ

rows.rule: The §1014 basis adjustment generally does not apply to assets of an irrevocable grantor trust that are not included in the deceased grantor's gross estate.
rows.impact: Have counsel confirm the trust type. A revocable living trust (included in the estate) is the usual vehicle that keeps the step-up.
rows.source: IRS — Internal Revenue Bulletin 2023-16, Rev. Rul. 2023-2

rows.rule: Up to $250,000 ($500,000 joint) of gain on a main home excluded if owned and used as a residence 24 of the last 60 months.
rows.impact: Relevant if an heir lives in an inherited house for 2+ years, then sells after it appreciates beyond the stepped-up basis.
rows.source: IRS — Topic no. 701, Sale of your home

rows.rule: 0% / 15% / 20% by taxable income (2025 thresholds listed on page); unrecaptured §1250 gain up to 25%; NIIT may also apply.
rows.impact: Applies to gain above the stepped-up basis when a house or reinvested portfolio is sold.
rows.source: IRS — Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses

rows.topic: Pending: full repeal of estate tax (S.587 / H.R.1301, 119th Congress)
rows.rule: Death Tax Repeal Act bills would repeal the estate and GST taxes.
rows.status_as_of: Introduced 02/13/2025; referred to committee; no further action shown
rows.impact: Not law. If ever enacted, federal estate tax exposure would disappear; plan on current law.
rows.source: Congress.gov — S.587 all actions

rows.rule: Death Tax Repeal Act (House).
rows.status_as_of: Introduced 02/13/2025; referred to Ways and Means; no further action shown
rows.impact: Not law. Monitor only.
rows.source: Congress.gov — H.R.1301 all actions

rows.rule: No California estate tax return is required for decedents dying on or after January 1, 2005; inheritance tax applies only to deaths before June 8, 1982.
rows.impact: No state-level death tax on the inheritance.
rows.source: California State Controller — California Estate Tax

rows.rule: Only the transferor's principal residence qualifies; it must become the child's principal residence within 1 year; homeowners' exemption must be filed within 1 year; claim within 3 years or before transfer to a third party. New taxable value = taxable value + (market value - (taxable value + $1M as adjusted)) when market value exceeds that sum.
rows.impact: The decisive property-tax rule for the inherited home: moving in preserves part of the low base; renting or holding vacant triggers full reassessment to market value.
rows.source: California Legislative Information — R&TC §63.2

rows.rule: $1,044,586 for transfers Feb 16, 2025 – Feb 15, 2027 (adjusted every other year by FHFA California HPI; up 2.15% from $1,022,600).
rows.status_as_of: Next adjustment due for transfers from Feb 16, 2027 (not yet published at check)
rows.impact: Grows with California house prices, so it will be larger by 2040–2050, but the formula still taxes everything above taxable value + exclusion.
rows.source: BOE — News Release NR 25-02 (LTA 2025/009)

rows.rule: Base year values rise by CCPI change capped at 2%; 2026 roll factor 1.02 (CCPI +3.307%, capped).
rows.impact: Assessed value of a home not reassessed grows at most 2%/yr; full 2% applied in 2017–2020 and 2022–2026 rolls.
rows.source: BOE — Letter To Assessors No. 2026/002

rows.rule: $7,000 reduction in taxable value for an owner-occupied principal residence; one-time claim on BOE-266; file by February 15 for full-year exemption.
rows.impact: Required within 1 year to keep the Prop 19 exclusion (see L13). Worth about $7,000 x local rate per year.
rows.source: BOE — Homeowners' Exemption

rows.topic: Failed 2026 initiative to repeal Prop 19 inheritance rules (No. 25-0017)
rows.rule: Would have restored pre-Prop 19 parent-child exclusions from Jan 1, 2027. Petition failed: signatures filed were below the number required (SOS memo #26138, May 18, 2026).
rows.impact: Prop 19 rules remain in force. Treat any future repeal attempt as upside only, not a planning assumption.
rows.source: CA Secretary of State — CC/ROV Memorandum #26138

rows.rule: LAO: measure would reverse most Prop 19 changes; revenue loss ~ $1B/yr initially rising to ~ $2B/yr.
rows.impact: Shows the scale of revenue at stake, a reason repeal is politically difficult.
rows.source: Legislative Analyst's Office — A.G. File No. 25-0017

rows.rule: SOS list of initiatives cleared for circulation (checked 2026-11-10) shows five measures (26-0001 to 26-0005); none concerns Prop 19 or inherited-property reassessment.
rows.impact: No active Prop 19 change in the pipeline. Re-check before the 2028 cycle.
rows.source: CA Secretary of State — Initiatives cleared for circulation

rows.rule: Makes Prop 30 higher income-tax rates on high incomes permanent instead of expiring in 2031. Unofficial result: Yes 60.6% (as of Nov 9, 2026; certification by Dec 11, 2026).
rows.impact: CA income tax applies to profits from selling property and investments; higher top brackets continue for large sale gains and portfolio income after 2030.
rows.source: CA SOS — Statewide ballot measure results; LAO analysis (Voter Guide)

rows.rule: One-time tax on certain taxpayers. Unofficial result: No 52.8%.
rows.impact: No direct effect on this household's decision.
rows.source: CA SOS — Statewide ballot measure results

rows.topic: Nov 3, 2026 — Prop 42 (bars new state personal-property taxes)
rows.rule: Prohibits new state taxes on ownership of financial assets or other personal property and limits retroactive taxes. Unofficial result: Yes 51.6%.
rows.impact: If certified, a future state wealth tax on stock/savings holdings would be barred — modestly favours the sell-and-reinvest path.
rows.source: CA Voter Guide — LAO analysis of Prop 42

rows.topic: Nov 3, 2026 — Prop 43 (2/3 vote for voter-initiated local special taxes)
rows.rule: Legislative constitutional amendment. Unofficial result: No 57.3%.
rows.impact: Local parcel taxes can still be passed by citizen initiative at current thresholds — fixed charges on property tax bills may keep rising.
rows.source: CA SOS — Statewide ballot measure results

rows.rule: Documentary transfer tax does not apply to a deed transferring realty by reason of death, outright or in trust (R&TC §11930).
rows.impact: Distributing the house from the trust to the heir triggers no county/city transfer tax; a later sale does.
rows.source: California Legislative Information — R&TC §11930

rows.topic: County documentary transfer tax rate on a sale
rows.rule: County rate $0.55 per $500 of consideration (= $1.10 per $1,000); a city in that county may levy half that amount, credited against the county tax. Charter-city rates (e.g., San Francisco) are set locally and are not covered by this row.
rows.impact: On a sale, budget the county rate at minimum; SF's own rate schedule must be checked separately (not verified here).
rows.source: California Legislative Information — R&TC §11911

rows.rule: NEM 2.0 customers may stay on NEM 2.0 for 20 years from interconnection (D.14-03-041); new interconnections since Apr 15, 2023 take the Net Billing Tariff, whose export credits are usually lower than retail rates.
rows.impact: A system interconnected before 2023 loses NEM terms ~20 years after interconnection — likely before a 2040–2050 inheritance. Do not assume today's ~$0 electric bill / monthly credit continues.
rows.source: CPUC — Net Energy Metering and Net Billing
